rules.rule: A brightness gradient across a flat surface indicates falloff; steepness implies a close source while flatness implies a distant one.
rules.evidence: A brightness gradient across a plain flat surface with no object causing it. Steep means a close source.

rules.rule: If the near and far sides of an object show a large drop in light, the source is likely within a metre or two.
rules.evidence: Compare the near and far side of one object. A big drop across a head means a source a metre or two away.

rules.rule: A background that is pitch black relative to a nearby subject indicates a close light source, not a dark object.
rules.evidence: A background far darker than the subject with nothing else explaining it — used deliberately, the cheapest way to separate subject from surroundings (Value structure).
